items.item_text: Active California Certified Nursing Assistant Certificate (CNA) OR transcripts from your current enrollment in a BSN/MSN program with at least one completed Med Surg rotation, required
Clerical experience in an acute hospital environment, preferred

There’s nothing more exciting and rewarding than being able to make a significant, positive difference in someone’s life. At UCLA Health, you’ll experience this joy every day while also enjoying the positive, supportive, and collaborative environment that makes ours one of the most loved workplaces. Join us and find out for yourself.

We are seeking a compassionate and dedicated Administrative Clinical Care Partner to join our team, playing a vital role in delivering high-quality patient care while supporting healthcare professionals across a variety of medical settings. Working within the Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA) scope of practice, you will assist patients throughout the continuum of care, including admission, transfer, and discharge processes; support personal hygiene; assist with meals and excretory needs; and help ensure patient safety, comfort, and overall well-being. In addition to direct patient care, you may also provide clerical and administrative support to the designated unit to help maintain efficient daily operations.

The ideal candidate will demonstrate empathy, excellent communication skills, and the ability to work efficiently and collaboratively with others to deliver compassionate, cutting-edge patient care while contributing to a positive and supportive team environment at UCLA Health.
This position floats to various units within the UCLA Health system below based on the patient census and the skills of the staff. Hospital locations include but are not limited to the following:
Understanding of basic medical terminology and abbreviations, preferred
Ability to complete an 8-hour computer data entry training course
Ability to perform all delegated nursing and PT/OT/RT assisted tasks
Ability to work efficiently and effectively with others
Skill in evaluating and reporting emergent patient/unit information
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment under a heavy workload
